findings.minimal_remediation: Extend duplicate-ownership coverage with F2P apply-failure cases for two ansibleops_line and two ansibleops_block resources that share the same path and name (distinct Terraform resource addresses).

findings.why_it_matters: Instruction and resource-reference define line and block external identities as path plus stable name, and the general one-key-per-resource rule requires rejecting duplicate claims. evidence.observation: Advanced systems task with workdir /app/provider, separate verifier environment, and 8192MB memory; tags terraform/ansible/provider/state-reconciliation indicating a provider-completion work package.
Primary entrypoint serves terraform-provider-ansibleops via hashicorp terraform-plugin-framework providerserver at registry.terraform.io/local/ansibleops.

Registers ten resource constructors (file, directory, copy, template, line, block, symlink, user, group, cron), configures runtime from provider schema, and runs validateRuntimePreflight before exposing ResourceData.

241-line preflight inspects inventory size/group/host constraints, resolves executable ansible-playbook, probes temp_dir writability via MkdirTemp/write/read/remove, and bounds mutation timeout to 1s–1h whole seconds.

ProcessRunner validates absolute inventory/temp paths, writes ephemeral playbooks under TempDir, executes ansible-playbook with timeout/context cancellation, merges env overrides, captures exit codes, and removes playbooks on success.
Single mutation path renders SingleTask playbooks and delegates to configured Runner with ANSIBLE_NOCOLOR and ANSIBLE_HOST_KEY_CHECKING env overrides.
Read-side InspectPath uses lstat, symlink readlink, optional SHA-256 digest, UID/GID to owner/group resolution, and file kind classification without invoking Ansible.
InspectCron scans /var/spool/cron paths for #Ansible markers, parses schedule fields, and detects disabled entries—distinct observation logic from path/account modules.
InspectUser/InspectGroup combine user.Lookup with /etc/passwd and /etc/group parsing for shell, supplementary groups, and member lists.
ChangeSet supports mode-normalized diffs, canonical slice comparison, DiffPath and DiffCron helpers used to gate updates before mutation.
Representative path resource: Create/Update invoke ansible.FileTask, Read uses observe.InspectPath only, Update applies lifecycle.DiffPath before selective mutation, Delete uses absent state.
Line resource validates Unix names and managed lines, uses ansible.LineTask for mutation, and refreshes observed_exact_count/observed_regexp_count via observe.InspectLine.

Documents read/mutation separation, content digest-driven updates, scoped deletes for line/block/cron siblings, symlink target preservation, and remove_home_on_destroy behavior—cross-resource partial-fix traps.

Operator workflow runs gofmt, local go build with trimpath/ldflags, installs provider binary to filesystem mirror under /opt/terraform/plugins/registry.terraform.io/local/ansibleops/0.1.0/linux_amd64.
End-to-end operator smoke builds provider, terraform init/apply/destroy on examples/basic/main.tf, and asserts managed filesystem artifacts under /tmp/ansibleops-smoke-managed.

Pins golang base digest and terraform 1.10.5 checksum, installs ansible-core and runtime tooling, vendors Go modules, builds provider via build-provider.sh, and configures TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE/ANSIBLE_CONFIG env defaults.

role_output.PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Fixing only mutation paths while leaving read-side observe stale; updating file/directory resources without lifecycle.DiffPath short-circuit semantics; line/block/cron scoped deletes that must not remove sibling-owned entries; symlink delete vs target preservation; user destroy with remove_home_on_destroy; template/copy updates requiring source_digest or variables_fingerprint changes; provider Configure preflight failures blocking all resources.
role_output.REMOVAL_TEST: Removing ~25% of core (e.g., observe/account+cron modules plus three resource families and preflight probes) would eliminate distinct account/cron observation, inventory/binary validation, and multiple managed-object lifecycles—materially reducing provider behavior rather than cosmetic dead code.
role_output.SUBSTANTIVE_LOC_ASSESSMENT: ~2,964 lines of reachable Go across cmd/internal plus ~132 lines of build/runtime configuration (Dockerfile, shell entrypoints, ansible/terraform config, basic example) for ~3,096 substantive solver-visible runtime/config LOC; excludes go.mod and markdown docs; meets the large_system_strict 3,000-line floor.

Q6_RESULT.summary: The solver-visible environment is a reachable Terraform provider stack that mutates local Linux state through Ansible while observing drift natively on read. Ten differentiated resource lifecycles, preflight validation, subprocess execution control, and cross-cutting lifecycle invariants provide credible production coupling and partial-fix traps; repetitive resource scaffolding is present but domain-justified and not empty padding. Substantive runtime/configuration LOC in the environment tree (~3,096 lines of Go plus build/runtime config) meets the large_system_strict floor.
